title: Credit Card Web Portal Redesign · First PREMIER Bank
jpTitle: クレジットカード Web ポータル リデザイン

summary.en: Led a discovery audit of First PREMIER Bank's credit card portal that found the root cause was a total absence of design infrastructure, not cosmetic issues. Prioritized 4 of 10 flows for rebuild — account setup, login, summary, payments — and built a 125+ component design system in three layers, later adopted org-wide.
summary.jp: First PREMIER 銀行のカードポータルを監査した。原因は見た目でなく設計基盤の不在だった。優先 4 業務を再構築し、125 超の部品からなる仕組みを作った。後に全社標準となった。

product.en: The audit's finding wasn't a list of broken screens — it was that there was no shared component layer at all, so any fix would regress. The two-part response — rebuild four priority flows, then build the 125+ component system underneath — addressed both the symptom and the cause.
product.jp: 監査で見つかったのは、壊れた画面の一覧ではなかった。共通の部品層が丸ごと無いという事実だった。優先 4 業務の作り直しと部品体系づくりを同時に進めた。

business.en: A design system built for one bank portal was later adopted by an unrelated team (mobile app v2.0) and then became the org-wide standard — evidence the underlying architecture, not just the four rebuilt flows, was the actual deliverable.
business.jp: 1 つの銀行向けに作った部品体系を、別のモバイルアプリチームが採用した。やがて全社標準になった。本当の成果は、その下にある設計基盤だった。

mine: Led the discovery audit to find the structural root cause rather than catalog every individual problem

narrative.problem: The portal had been built incrementally over years: the same account information appeared in multiple places with different interaction patterns, users couldn't complete basic tasks like making a payment without redundant screens, and service call volume was climbing because users couldn't self-serve.
built: Rebuilt account setup, login, summary and payments flows
125+ component design system in 3 layers: Foundation, Components, Patterns

business: Service calls decreased in 2022 as streamlined payment and account flows removed friction
The mobile app team adopted the same system for their 2022 v2.0 release
The system became the org-wide design standard by 2023+

name.jp: クレジットカード・ポータル

oneLiner.en: A bank's credit card portal, rebuilt on a design system.
oneLiner.jp: 銀行のクレジットカード・ポータルを、デザインシステムから作り直した。

challenge.en: The portal had grown piece by piece for years: the same account data in three-plus places with different patterns, five-plus clicks to make a payment, no shared components. Customers couldn't self-serve, so service calls climbed — in an interface where you are asking people to move their money.
challenge.jp: ポータルは何年もかけて継ぎ足されてきた。同じ口座情報が 3 か所以上に別々の形で出てきて、支払いには 5 回以上のクリックが要り、共通の部品はひとつもない。自分で済ませられないから、問い合わせの電話が増えていく。お金を動かしてもらう画面なのに。

solution.en: A discovery audit showed the cause wasn't cosmetic: there was no design infrastructure at all. So the fix ran on two levels — rebuild the four flows that hurt most (account setup, login, summary, payments) and build a 125+ component system in three layers. The decisive move was treating the system as the deliverable. The mobile team adopted it, and by 2023 it was the org-wide standard.
solution.jp: 調べてわかったのは、原因が見た目ではなく、デザインの基盤そのものが無いことだった。だから直し方を 2 段にした。いちばん痛い 4 つのフロー（口座開設、ログイン、概要、支払い）を作り直し、125 超の部品を 3 層でまとめたシステムを組む。決め手は、フローではなくシステムを成果物として扱ったこと。モバイルチームが採用し、2023 年には全社の標準になった。
